native_ownership.responsibility: Design a product AI agent's smallest sufficient state, least-privilege tools, resource authorization, approvals, idempotent effects, memory governance, observability and evaluation without recreating native Codex orchestration.
excludes: Native Codex planning, skills, approvals, sandbox, memory, plugins, multi-agent communication and subagent lifecycle are Codex-owned and out of scope.
Conversational UI implementation is owned by chatbot-implement.
Prompt templates without agent-system architecture are owned by prompt-engineering.

risk.rationale: This architecture skill produces design decisions only and must not mutate repository files, providers, memory stores, tools, or external systems.

positive.prompt: Design the smallest product agent for tenant-scoped support actions. Specify resource authorization, exact-parameter approvals, idempotent operations, unknown-outcome reconciliation, memory consent/provenance/deletion and executable adversarial evaluation.

Design a read-only research agent that retrieves user-consented long-term memory and business sources while preventing poisoned instructions and cross-tenant influence, with explicit provenance, correction, retention and deletion.

negative.prompt: Implement a secure multi-tenant chatbot UI and server route with installed AI SDK transport, authoritative messages, streaming rendering, tools, persistence and handoff.
Create deterministic structured prompts, schemas, examples and output validation for an existing automation whose runtime, tools, authorization and memory architecture are already decided.

scenarios.prompt: An agent architecture grants one broad tenant credential to every tool, trusts prompt sanitization to stop injection, retries duplicate tool calls, uses ask_llm when approval times out and selects fixed iteration/token counts copied from a blog. Produce a read-only correction.

assertions.criterion: Designs a product agent only, remains read-only, and does not recreate, configure or claim ownership of native Codex orchestration.
Inspects provider/runtime, auth/data/tool boundaries, organizational policy, evaluation evidence and installed stack from the fixture while separating facts from assumptions.
Starts with deterministic or single-call options, adds agent boundaries only for measured gaps, then defines state, tools, auth, approval, effects, memory, observability and rollout.

Uses resource-scoped authorization and least privilege, treats prompts/retrieval as untrusted, binds approval to exact parameters and operation, fails closed instead of ask_llm, reconciles duplicate/unknown effects and derives limits from SLO/provider/evaluation evidence.
Defines executable cases for injection, resource substitution, stale permission, approval swaps, duplicate tool delivery, timeout after success, limit exhaustion and kill/rollback behavior.
Reports trust/data boundaries, smallest architecture, state/tool/auth/approval/effect contracts, evidence-derived limits, memory policy, evaluation and rollout risks.
Avoids arbitrary topology, agent counts and budgets, keeps capabilities modular and gives each planner/memory/delegation boundary a measured rationale and removal path.

scenarios.prompt: A shared memory store contains an unverified instruction saved from tenant A. Retrieval injects it into tenant B's agent, which requests deleting a resource; approval names only the tool, not parameters, and the provider times out after success. Define the safe architecture.

assertions.criterion: Rejects cross-tenant memory and unbound approval, requires tenant/user/purpose partition, provenance, current resource authorization, exact normalized target/version and durable operation identity before any deletion.
Treats retrieved instruction as untrusted evidence, invalidates changed approval parameters, reconciles provider state after timeout and prevents duplicate deletion rather than blindly retrying.
Requires memory isolation/deletion tests, approval audit binding, provider-authoritative resource state and one effective operation across timeout/duplicate delivery.
Reports poisoned memory provenance and remediation, approval denial, reconciled external state and any unresolved provider boundary without exposing tenant data.

scenarios.prompt: A proposed design assumes current AI SDK tool approval and multi-step APIs, but the repository pins an older supported line. The architecture request does not authorize migration.

assertions.criterion: Uses ai-sdk project detection, lockfile, installed tool/approval types, provider capability and matching docs; designs a capability-compatible boundary and separates migration.
Checks AI core/provider SDK, runtime, persistence/checkpoint store, auth service and evaluation harness together.
Keeps version-specific AI SDK mechanics behind capability interfaces and avoids remembered majors, removal dates or fixed budgets.

provenance.claim_scope: prompt injection is not solved by prompt sanitization
AI SDK tool validation and approval flow
